# Prerequisites

_BiocStyle_ includes a [Quarto](https://quarto.org) extension, `biocstyle`,
that gives Quarto documents the _Bioconductor_ style, and two vignette
engines that build `.qmd` vignettes with it. Building a Quarto vignette
needs

- the Quarto command line tool (see the [installation
  instructions](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/)),
- the `r CRANpkg("quarto")` _R_ package, and
- `r CRANpkg("knitr")` and `r CRANpkg("rmarkdown")`, which Quarto uses to run
  _R_ code.

This vignette is itself a Quarto vignette built with `BiocStyle::quarto_html`.
Its companion, "Authoring R Markdown vignettes", describes the
R Markdown formats `BiocStyle::html_document` and `BiocStyle::pdf_document`.

# Getting started

The quickest start is `use_vignette_quarto()`, run from the package
directory:

```{r}
#| eval: false
BiocStyle::use_vignette_quarto("MyPackage")              # HTML
BiocStyle::use_vignette_quarto("MyPackage-pdf", "pdf")   # PDF
```

It creates `vignettes/<name>.qmd` with the vignette header and the outline of
a package vignette (installation, support and session information), and calls
`use_quarto_extension()` so that the vignette can be previewed (see
@sec-preview).

To set up a Quarto vignette by hand:

- Edit the `DESCRIPTION` file by adding

        VignetteBuilder: BiocStyle
        Suggests: BiocStyle, knitr, quarto

  If the package also has R Markdown vignettes, use
  `VignetteBuilder: BiocStyle, knitr`.

- Use the format `biocstyle-html` or `biocstyle-pdf`, and the matching
  vignette engine, in the document header:

        ---
        title: "Vignette Title"
        author: "Vignette Author"
        package: PackageName
        format: biocstyle-html
        vignette: >
          %\VignetteIndexEntry{Vignette Title}
          %\VignetteEngine{BiocStyle::quarto_html}
          %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
        ---

  For PDF output use `format: biocstyle-pdf` and
  `%\VignetteEngine{BiocStyle::quarto_pdf}`.

When the package is built, the engine copies the `biocstyle` extension of the
installed _BiocStyle_ next to the vignette, renders the vignette with
`quarto::quarto_render()`, and removes the copy again. So the package does not
carry a copy of the extension, and vignettes always get the style of the
installed _BiocStyle_. If the `quarto` _R_ package or the Quarto command line
tool is missing, building the vignette fails, except under `R CMD check`,
where the engine warns and writes a placeholder instead.

## Previewing a vignette {#sec-preview}

`quarto render` and the RStudio "Render" button do not go through the
vignette engine, so they need the extension in `vignettes/_extensions`.
`use_quarto_extension()` copies it there:

```{r}
#| eval: false
BiocStyle::use_quarto_extension("vignettes")
```

The copy is only for previewing, so the function adds
`vignettes/_extensions` (and the `Bioconductor.sty` file that rendering to PDF
leaves next to the document) to the package's `.Rbuildignore` and
`.gitignore`. Run it again with `overwrite = TRUE` after updating
_BiocStyle_. When previewing, the version in the package line (see
@sec-header) is read from the package's `DESCRIPTION` file.

# R Markdown and Quarto features

@tbl-features maps the features of the R Markdown formats to their Quarto
counterparts. Most of the Quarto features are Quarto's own; the `biocstyle`
formats turn them on by default and style them.

| R Markdown (_BiocStyle_) | Quarto (`biocstyle` extension) |
|:-------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| `output: BiocStyle::html_document` | `format: biocstyle-html` |
| `output: BiocStyle::pdf_document` | `format: biocstyle-pdf` (uses the same `Bioconductor.sty`) |
| `%\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}` | `%\VignetteEngine{BiocStyle::quarto_html}` or `BiocStyle::quarto_pdf` |
| `use_vignette_html()`, `use_vignette_pdf()` | `use_vignette_quarto(format = "html")` or `"pdf"` |
| `author:` with `name`, `affiliation`, `email` | the same fields, following Quarto's [author schema](https://quarto.org/docs/journals/authors.html) |
| `abstract:` | `abstract:` |
| `package:` adds "Package: _name version_" | `package:` (same) |
| `date:` defaults to today | `date:` defaults to today |
| Floating table of contents (`toc_float: true`) | on by default, on the left (`toc-location: left`) |
| Numbered sections | on by default (`number-sections: true`) |
| Footnotes as sidenotes | footnotes in the margin (`reference-location: margin`) |
| `fig.small = TRUE` | chunk option `classes: fig-small` (with `fig-width: 5`) |
| `fig.wide = TRUE` | chunk option `classes: fig-wide` (with `fig-width: 10`), or Quarto's `column: page-right` |
| Horizontally scrolling wide tables | same, tables are wrapped in a scrolling container |
| `Biocpkg()`, `CRANpkg()`, `Githubpkg()` in inline _R_ code | the same inline _R_ code |
| `\@ref(fig:label)` (_bookdown_) | `@fig-label`, `@tbl-label`, `@sec-label` |
| `BiocStyle::md_document` | Quarto's `gfm` format |

: R Markdown features of _BiocStyle_ and their Quarto equivalents. {#tbl-features}

# Document header {#sec-header}

## Authors and affiliations

The `author` field takes author names with affiliations and emails, as in
Quarto's [author schema](https://quarto.org/docs/journals/authors.html).
A single author can be a character string

    author: "Single Author"

and several authors with affiliations and emails a list:

    author:
      - name: First Author
        affiliations:
          - Shared affiliation
          - Additional affiliation
      - name: Second Author
        affiliation: Shared affiliation
        email: corresponding@author.com

As in `BiocStyle::html_document`, the formats list unique affiliations below
the authors, with numbers linking authors to their affiliations, and emails
marked with asterisks. Quarto's other author fields (ORCID, roles, ...) are
accepted but not shown.

## Abstract, package and date

The `abstract` field is shown under an "Abstract" heading. The `package` field
should contain the package name; it is shown under a "Package" heading
together with the package version, as at the top of this document. When the
vignette is built, the engine takes the version from the package being built
(or, for a package other than the one being built, from the installed
package). The `date` defaults to the date the document is rendered; set
`date:` to override it.

# Style macros

`r Biocpkg("BiocStyle")` provides the following macros for referring to
_R_ packages. Call them with inline _R_ code; the vignette has to load
_BiocStyle_ first, for example in a setup chunk with `#| include: false`.

```{r}
#| include: false
macro <- function(name, pkg, description)
    sprintf('`%s("%s")` %s %s', name, pkg, description,
            do.call(name, list(pkg)))
inline <- function(cmd) sprintf('`` `r %s` ``', cmd)
```

* `r macro("Biocpkg", "IRanges", "for _Bioconductor_ software, annotation and experiment data packages, including a link to the package landing page,")`.

* `r macro("CRANpkg", "data.table", "for _R_ packages available on CRAN, including a link to the CRAN landing page,")`.

* `r macro("Githubpkg", "rstudio/rmarkdown", "for _R_ packages available on GitHub, including a link to the package repository,")`.

* `r macro("Rpackage", "MyPkg", "for _R_ packages that are _not_ available on _Bioconductor_, CRAN or GitHub.")`

For example, write `r inline('Biocpkg("IRanges")')` to get
`r Biocpkg("IRanges")`.

# Figures

## Regular figures

Figures with a caption are numbered, and can be referenced with Quarto's
cross-reference syntax: a chunk labelled `fig-cars` is referenced with
`@fig-cars`, as in @fig-cars.

```{{r}}
#| label: fig-cars
#| fig-cap: "Regular figure. A plot produced by a code chunk."
plot(cars)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-cars
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Regular figure. A plot produced by a code chunk."
plot(cars)
```

## Small and wide figures

The R Markdown chunk options `fig.small` and `fig.wide` become the figure
classes `fig-small` and `fig-wide`, set with the `classes` chunk option.
A small figure (@fig-small) is narrower than the text and centered; a wide
figure (@fig-wide) extends into the right margin. Unlike the R Markdown chunk
options, the classes do not change the size of the plot itself, so set
`fig-width` to match: 5 inches for small and 10 inches for wide figures (the
formats default to 8 by 5 inches).

```{{r}}
#| label: fig-small
#| classes: fig-small
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-cap: "Small figure. A plot produced by a code chunk with `classes: fig-small`."
plot(cars)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-small
#| echo: false
#| classes: fig-small
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-cap: "Small figure. A plot produced by a code chunk with `classes: fig-small`."
plot(cars)
```

```{{r}}
#| label: fig-wide
#| classes: fig-wide
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-cap: "Wide figure. A plot produced by a code chunk with `classes: fig-wide`."
plot(pressure, type = "b")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-wide
#| echo: false
#| classes: fig-wide
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-cap: "Wide figure. A plot produced by a code chunk with `classes: fig-wide`."
plot(pressure, type = "b")
```

The classes also work on Markdown images, e.g.
`![Caption](image.png){.fig-small}`. For other layouts, use Quarto's
[`column` option](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html);
`fig-wide` is a shortcut for `column: page-right`.

## Alternative text

Captions are used as the alternative text of figures. To describe a figure
for screen readers in other words, or to describe a figure without a caption,
use the `fig-alt` chunk option.

# Tables

Tables, from Markdown or from _R_ code such as `knitr::kable()`, are wrapped
in a container that scrolls horizontally, so that wide tables, like
@tbl-wide, do not overflow the page.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-wide
#| tbl-cap: "A wide table."
wide <- as.data.frame(matrix(round(seq(-1, 1, length.out = 60), 2), nrow = 3))
knitr::kable(wide)
```

# Footnotes and margin notes

Footnotes appear in the margin next to the text that refers to
them.^[Like this footnote, written as `^[text of the footnote]`.] Other
content can be put in the margin with the `.column-margin` class:

    ::: {.column-margin}
    A note in the margin.
    :::

::: {.column-margin}
A note in the margin.
:::

In PDF output, footnotes are placed as by `BiocStyle::pdf_document`.

# PDF output

`format: biocstyle-pdf` uses `Bioconductor.sty`, the LaTeX style file of
`BiocStyle::pdf_document`, and adds the title block (authors, affiliations,
emails, abstract and package version) and a table of contents on its own
page. It compiles with `pdflatex` by default; set `pdf-engine` to change
that. `fig-small` and `fig-wide` work in PDF output too.

```{r}
#| label: session-info
#| echo: false
sessionInfo()
```
